ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a small circular rolling object at the lower left, moving with speed v toward the right along a fixed track that curves upward. A dashed horizontal baseline marks the initial level, and a dashed vertical line at the right indicates the vertical height reached above that initial level. Reasoning: For pure rolling, the initial kinetic energy is translational plus rotational: (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)Iω^2. With rolling without slipping, ω = v/R. Write I = βmR^2, so the initial kinetic energy is (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)βmR^2(v^2/R^2) = (1/2)(1+β)mv^2. At maximum height the object is momentarily at rest, so this energy becomes gravitational potential energy mgh. Thus h = (1+β)v^2/(2g). Given h = 3v^2/(4g), equate: (1+β)/2 = 3/4, so 1+β = 3/2 and β = 1/2. A uniform object with moment of inertia I = (1/2)mR^2 about its symmetry axis is a solid disc.

method.method_draft: Use conservation of mechanical energy for pure rolling. From the image, note that the object is rolling up a fixed curved track and reaches a vertical height above its starting level. From the text, take the initial center-of-mass speed as v and the maximum rise as h = 3v^2/(4g). At maximum height the rolling object is momentarily at rest, so initial translational plus rotational kinetic energy becomes gravitational potential energy: (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)I(v/R)^2 = mgh. Write I = beta mR^2, giving h = (1+beta)v^2/(2g). Equate this to 3v^2/(4g), so beta = 1/2. Identify the uniform object with I = (1/2)mR^2 as a solid disc.

method.method_draft: Use rolling dynamics along the tangent rather than starting from energy. From the image, interpret the motion as a small circular rigid body rolling up a smooth curved ramp with changing slope; the relevant height is the vertical rise. From the text, use initial speed v and final height h = 3v^2/(4g). For a rolling body with I = beta mR^2, the tangential deceleration on an incline element is a = -g sin(theta)/(1+beta). Along the curved surface, use a = v dv/ds and dh = sin(theta) ds, then integrate from initial speed v to final speed 0: v^2/2 = gh/(1+beta). Thus h = (1+beta)v^2/(2g). Comparing with 3v^2/(4g) gives beta = 1/2, so the object is the uniform disc.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个小圆形刚体在左下方沿水平处进入一条向右上方弯曲升高的轨道，旁边标有初速度 v；右端用竖直虚线表示相对于初始位置的最大竖直高度。由此可知问题中的高度是竖直升高量，物体是在曲面上纯滚动上升。

按切向滚动动力学处理。设物体转动惯量 I = beta mR^2。对任意一小段倾角为 theta 的轨道，纯滚动时沿切向的加速度为 a = -g sin(theta)/(1 + beta)。又因为 a = u du/ds，且竖直高度增量 dh = sin(theta) ds，所以 u du/ds = -g/(1 + beta) * dh/ds。积分从初速度 v 到最高点速度 0、从高度 0 到 h，得到 v^2/2 = gh/(1 + beta)，即 h = (1 + beta)v^2/(2g)。题给 h = 3v^2/(4g)，所以 (1 + beta)/2 = 3/4，解得 beta = 1/2。均匀圆盘的转动惯量为 I = (1/2)mR^2，因此该物体是圆盘。
